steps.title: Rich and subtle
steps.body: Marsanne gives full-bodied whites with pear, quince, honeysuckle, almond and, with age, honey and nuts. Acidity is low to medium, alcohol moderate to high, texture waxy and rich. It's less aromatic than Viognier, more about texture than perfume.

steps.title: Origins
steps.body: Marsanne takes its name from the village of Marsanne, near Montélimar in the Rhône. It's a northern Rhône grape, closely linked to Roussanne, its frequent blending partner. It's more productive and reliable than Roussanne, but can be flabby if overcropped or picked too late.

steps.explanation: Marsanne is full-bodied and waxy, more about texture than aroma.

steps.title: Spotting it
steps.body: Look for medium lemon to gold colour, a subtle nose of pear, almond and flowers, and a full, waxy palate with low to moderate acidity. Young, it can seem quiet; with age, it develops honey and nutty notes. Compared with Viognier, it's less perfumed and less apricot.

steps.prompt: Marsanne is more aromatic than Viognier.
steps.explanation: Not true. Viognier is far more perfumed. Marsanne is about texture.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Marsanne gives pear, almond and a waxy texture
It's named after a Rhône village and pairs with Roussanne
It's subtle young and honeyed with age
